title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). S is smooth and irreducible over Q with function field K. U_S → S is an 'elementary' (Artin-neighbourhood) fibration with successive anabelian fibres. Write E_X for the arithmetic fundamental group π1(X). A rational section f of U over S gives a section of E_{U_K} → E_K. Equivalently, it gives a lift E_K → E_{U_S} of the surjection E_K → E_S. Grothendieck wants a section-conjecture-type statement: f is everywhere defined iff the Galois section is 'unramified over S'. That means the lift E_K → E_{U_S} kills the kernel of E_K → E_S, i.e. factors through E_S.

This page shows that this unramifiedness condition is of codimension 1 on S.
(i) Let Y ⊂ S be closed of codimension ≥ 2 and S' = S∖Y. Zariski–Nagata purity gives π1(S') ≅ π1(S). Hence ker(E_K → E_S) = ker(E_K → E_{S'}).
(ii) Cover S' by good opens S'_i (the text reads 'modèles' or 'modulaires', presumably elementary or K(π,1) neighbourhoods). Then ker(E_K → E_{S'}) is the closed subgroup generated by the kernels of E_K → E_{S'_i}.
(iii) Consequently, if the Galois section is unramified over each S'_i, it is unramified over S. The S'_i need only cover S', not S.

The next page draws the conclusion. To prove the equivalence 'unramified section ⇔ everywhere-defined rational point', one also needs the geometric counterpart: a section of U_S over S' extends to S. Using the elementary fibration, this reduces step by step to a relative hyperbolic curve X−T with T split. For genus ≥ 1, Weil's extension theorem extends the section into X. Then f^{-1}(T) is a divisor vanishing off a codimension-≥2 set, hence zero. So the proposed strategy is: section conjecture over a higher-dimensional base, i.e. integral versus rational sections, reduced to codimension-1 and curve statements.
errors: Step (ii) is stated without proof but is correct. Each ker(E_K→E_{S'_i}) is normal and contained in ker(E_K→E_{S'}). Conversely, a finite étale cover of Spec K that extends over every S'_i extends over S' by gluing normalizations. Equivalently, purity identifies these kernels as normal closures of inertia at codimension-1 points, and every divisor of S' meets some S'_i.
The direction 'everywhere defined ⇒ factorization' is trivial. The page only localizes the converse; it does not prove it.

The genus-0 case is not addressed on this page. For P^1 minus at least 3 split sections, a codimension-2 extension needs a separate argument, since rational maps to P^1 need not extend in codimension 2. It does hold here, via Hartogs for units, but is not written.

ideas.what: Unramifiedness of a Galois section over a regular base is a codimension-1 (local) condition, via Zariski–Nagata purity and gluing over an open cover
ideas.modern_name: Purity for the étale fundamental group / local nature of unramified sections

ideas.what: Section conjecture over a higher-dimensional base: a rational section is integral (everywhere defined) iff the associated Galois section is unramified over S, reduced to relative curves via elementary fibrations
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture for elementary anabelian varieties / relative section conjecture, integral points vs unramified sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Letter to Faltings 1983); later Stix and others on sections and ramification
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), which mentions reduction of anabelian statements for elementary varieties to curves; details unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful working-out of the purity reduction in Grothendieck's programme for the section conjecture over higher-dimensional bases. The ideas, purity and the elementary-fibration reduction to curves, are standard and match the Faltings letter and the later literature (e.g. Stix). It is a mildly interesting unpublished detail, but nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'sinon[?] préciser[?] (comme S' ... [?] par une "modulaire")' more plausibly reads 'or, on peut préciser (comme S' est recouvert par des "modèles")'. The word in quotes looks like 'modèle(s)' rather than 'modulaire'; likewise 'ouverts "modèles"' rather than '"modulaires"'.
'[-alors-] alors' should be '[-alors-] alors,' with the second word being a rewritten 'alors'.
'(qui pourraient [-ne pas-] ne recouvrent pas S, seulement S')' is better rendered as 'qui pourraient ne pas recouvrir S, seulement S''.
'ce qui est aussi signifier' likely reads 'ce qui est aussi signifier/dire que la condition…'; the reading is uncertain.
